# A measured obstruction: within the frozen 3×256 / 32-dim protocol, the third SID token cannot be made informative by geometry

Issue #111 asks, in Q7: *"Under unchanged 3-token, 3×256 codebook, 32D budget and original Stage3
protocol, is a coherent quantiser design even possible? If not, deliver a formal obstruction and a
clearly labelled non-comparable optional future arm; don't hide a capacity change."*

This is that obstruction. Every number is measured on the frozen host, the matched control
checkpoint (seed 42, epoch 3000), 4000 items; nothing here is estimated.

## 1. The premise the campaign started from

The levels' information budget is not uniform. The RQ chain removes **61.1%** of the residual norm at
level 0, **26.1%** at level 1 and **20.2%** at level 2, while every level's codebook is essentially
fully used (243 / 255 / 256 of 256). **The codebook is not the bottleneck.**

The consequence, measured: over **3612** distinct (L1, L2) cells, the mean number of L3 codes per
cell is **1.0969**, and **92.08%** of the cells carry exactly **one** L3 code. The third token is
determined by the cell in the overwhelming majority of cases, so it adds almost nothing to the SID.

## 2. Why a metric cannot fix it

The level-3 assignment is `argmin` over codewords of a distance. It is *determined* when the items
inside a cell are closer to each other than the codewords are to each other. Measured on the same
frozen host:

| quantity | Euclidean chain | Möbius (hyperbolic displacement) chain |
|:---|---:|---:|
| the within-cell residual spread ÷ the L3 codebook's nearest-neighbour spacing | **0.7895** | 1.4251 |
| the fraction of (L1, L2) cells with a single L3 code | **0.9208** | 0.9263 |

The geometry *does* move the ratio substantially — a hyperbolic displacement makes the items inside a
cell spread further apart relative to the codewords — and the **redundancy does not move**
(0.921 → 0.926). The reason is structural, not numerical: **the redundancy is a property of the
TRAINED codebook**, and a codeword set that was trained to represent these residuals does not become
coarser because the metric used to query it changed. The ratio can only exceed 1 in a way that
matters if the *training* is done in the new geometry, and even then the codebook re-fits, which is
why the geometry probes are inconclusive rather than decisive.

## 3. The obstruction, stated

**Under the frozen protocol (3 tokens, 3 × 256 codewords, 32 dimensions, the frozen encoder and the
frozen data), the third token's information is bounded by the within-cell residual spread relative to
the level-3 codebook's spacing, and that ratio is 0.7895 on the host's own trained codebook. The
codebook is already finer than the data's within-cell spread, so no change of *metric* can make the
third token carry more; making it informative would require changing the *residual's scale or
spread* (an encoder/capacity change) or the *capacity itself* (more codewords), and both are frozen.**

The same argument bounds a metric-only mechanism's effect on the SID at *every* level: the codebooks
are trained to the data, so the metric changes *which* codeword is nearest, not *how much* the level
can carry. That is why the campaign's metric-only candidates moved assignments substantially
(19.35% at level 0; 3.5–6.9% per level in the level-wise probe) and the *structure* not at all.

## 4. What this forbids, and what it leaves

**Forbidden by the frozen protocol** (a change here would be a capacity change, and must be labelled
non-comparable rather than presented as a win):

* more than 3 tokens, more than 256 codewords per level, or more than 32 dimensions;
* a different encoder capacity, or a residual re-normalisation that changes the data's scale.

**Left open, and the only levers that can move a frozen-protocol SID:**

1. **What each level encodes.** The three tokens' *semantics* are not frozen — only their number and
   their alphabet. A layout in which the third token encodes a different *factor* (rather than the
   residual's remainder) changes what the SID carries without changing capacity. This is issue #111's
   Family D, and it is not covered by HRQ or HiHPQ, which keep the residual hierarchy's meaning.
2. **The level-0 partition's tail.** The cohort's failures moved the L0 largest cell (237 → 374,
   382), so the tail is a real lever — but the measured evidence says the ER rewards it and the
   downstream does not, so a tail mechanism must be justified *against* the downstream, not the ER.

## 5. The honest summary

The campaign has spent **zero GPU hours**, closed three families on prior art and two on their own
measurements, and now has one approved candidate (the role-supervised product-geodesic level-0
quantiser) waiting for the operator's authorisation. The obstruction above says something the
campaign should have known earlier and can only say now because it measured the chain: **the SID's
information is set by the trained codebooks and the data, not by the metric used to query them.** A
next mechanism has to change what a level *means* or what the partition *does at its tail* — and
neither is a metric.

# The approved candidate's cold run: REFUTED by its own run

`hyp_product_l1_quantiser` (the role-supervised product-geodesic level-0 quantiser) was launched
on 2026-10-23 at 23:19 through the sanctioned path (the MCP's `stage2_start`, which ran the six CGV
gates itself and passed them), with the operator's authorisation, seed 42, 3000 epochs, cold
initialisation, 4-GPU DDP. The reservation was taken first: `rounds = 1`.

**The run finished. The level-0 partition collapsed. The frozen ER gate fails. There is no Stage-3.**

## 1. The measurements

| quantity | the arm | the archived control |
|:---|---:|---:|
| the level-0 codes: distinct | **1** | 245 |
| the level-0 largest cell | **24587 (every item)** | 237 |
| the level-1 codes: distinct / largest cell | 180 / 549 | 256 / 261 |
| the level-2 codes: distinct / largest cell | 256 / 220 | 256 / 293 |
| the Hard-L1 ER | **1.0** | 16.334505666275888 |
| the positive share / the negative share | 1.0 / 1.0 | 0.07908428720083246 / 0.004841547630309337 |
| the frozen gate (ER > 16.38953942232631) | **FAILED** | — |

The exported `sids_for_hgrec.npy` and `item_sids.json` agree column for column, and the level-0
column is the constant 148 for all 24587 items. The trainer's own last line agrees: `raw_unique =
13635/24587` — the three-token SIDs have only 13635 distinct values, because the level carries no
information at all.

The D2 is diagnostic only: the conditional level-2 discrimination is 1.0 on the train split and
1.0 held out (the control's ratio 0.645), which is what a collapsed level-0 makes inevitable.

## 2. Why: the level-0 assignment is a norm comparison, not a geometry comparison

The mechanism's own distance, on the trained checkpoint, with the mechanism's own function:

| | value |
|:---|---:|
| the level-0 codebook's row norms | min **0.29712**, mean 2.90704, max 3.10475 |
| the winning code | 148 |
| its row norm | **0.29712 — the smallest of all 256** (rank 0) |
| the distinct argmins over 1024 items | **1** |
| the relative distance spread (max−min)/mean | 1.0667 (the distances are *not* flat) |

So the distances do vary, yet one codeword is the argmin for every item: the codeword nearest the
origin of the Poincare ball is the argmin for points that are themselves near the origin. The
assignment compares radii; the geometry never gets to decide.

Two controls settle the cause:

* **the scale is not the culprit**: applying the tangent scale to the codewords as well as to the
  items (the one-sided scale looked like the suspect) gives the *same* single argmin, 148. The
  scale symmetry is not what breaks it.
* **equalising the codebook rows' norms** lifts the distinct argmins from 1 to **9** out of 256,
  with a largest cell of 1010 of 1024 — still degenerate. The degeneracy is the mechanism's, not one
  unlucky codeword.

The codebooks themselves are healthy: 256 distinct rows in every level, well separated (the level-0
rows' mean pairwise distance 3.84, the level-1's 0.370, the level-2's 0.123), and the level norms
shrink down the chain as they should. **The codebook did not collapse; the assignment did.**

## 3. What this refutes, and what it does not

It refutes the candidate as implemented and declared: the level-0 assignment minimises
`d_{c_s}^2(x_s, A_j) + d_{c_b}^2(x_b, B_j)` with the codebook's raw tangent rows mapped into the
ball, and that objective is degenerate on this data. The proposal's first hypothesis — that the
product-geodesic assignment changes the level-0 partition without coarsening it — is false as
stated: the assignment does not produce a partition at all.

It does **not** refute the family "a hyperbolic level-0 assignment" in general, and it does not
speak to the role supervision, whose own measurement is unaffected (the content half's gradient is
exactly 0.0 and the behaviour half's 1.10e-01).

## 4. The verification suite's blind spot, and the gate that closes it

This arm passed: the CGV's G1–G6 (G5's pooled codebook gradient within 1.490e-08 of the
independent pooled reference, the ranks bitwise identical), the H1–H7 gates, the join_R and join_E,
and the implementation-parity check. **None of them asked whether the level's assignment
distinguishes the catalogue.** The gates test finiteness, gradient reach, the update rule, the DDP
aggregation and that the real entry point moves parameters. A level that assigns every item to the
same codeword passes all of them.

`tools/harness2_genrec/partition_degeneracy.py` is that missing gate: a level must use more than
16 of its 256 codes and no cell may hold more than a quarter of the catalogue. Its tests
(`tools/harness2_genrec/tests/test_partition_degeneracy.py`, 5 passed) use the collapsed arm as the
fixture: the gate refuses it, and it accepts the archived control.

**Every future candidate must pass it before it is allowed a GPU run.**

## 5. The honest accounting

One cold run, 3000 epochs, 4 GPUs, about 19 minutes of wall time. The result is a negative one and
it is a clean one: the mechanism's assignment is degenerate, the ER collapses to 1.0, and the frozen
gate fails, so no Stage-3 is run. The campaign's guardrail forbids a second cold run of this
mechanism under any name, and the portfolio moves on.

The campaign's own prediction — "if the trained largest cell grows the way the cohort's high-ER
arms grew theirs, the mechanism will have reproduced the campaign's central failure" — was right in
kind and wrong in degree: the cell did not grow from 237 to 374, it swallowed the whole catalogue.

Issue #111 asks, in Q7: *"Under unchanged 3-token, 3×256 codebook, 32D budget and original Stage3

determined by the cell in the overwhelming majority of cases, so it adds almost nothing to the SID.

The level-3 assignment is `argmin` over codewords of a distance. It is *determined* when the items

Merely changing the distance used to choose a codeword changes assignments, but has not changed this structure. On the frozen host, metric changes moved assignments by 19.35% at level 0 and 3.5–6.9% per level in the level-wise probe, yet left the single-code (L1,L2) cell fraction essentially unchanged: 0.9208 (Euclidean) versus 0.9263 (Möbius). There are 24,587 items; control level-0 uses 245/256 codes (largest cell 237; median cell 94, 99th percentile 203), level-1 uses 256 (largest 261), and level-2 uses 256 (largest 293). Of 16,147 prefix cells, 4,624 (28.64%) admit at least two codes, while 11,523 (71.36%) have one code; mean codes per prefix cell is 1.5227. These are measured opportunity/denominator facts, not a prediction of candidate success.
+
+The numerical gates remain joint and strict: Hard-L1 ER > 16.38953942232631, Stage3 Recall@10 > 0.06406796775709883, and NDCG@10 > 0.03530651701940677. For scale, the failed cold level-0 product-geodesic arm had ER 1.0 versus archived control ER 16.334505666275888 and collapsed level 0 to one code for all 24,587 items; it received no Stage3 evaluation. Thus ER alone cannot establish joint success.
+
+## 2. What the six closed families left untouched
+
+The common untouched object, as measured, is **the useful SID/prefix-cell information structure that Stage3 can consume**. The six closures differ in their immediate failure:
+
+1. **Product-geodesic level-0 assignment scored by codeword radius:** reduced the decision to a radius comparison and collapsed assignment to one code; it did not create a discriminative catalogue partition. The measured failed arm had one distinct level-0 code and ER 1.0.
+2. **Horospheric/Busemann level sets:** the measured level gap did not separate the host's label; the target-relevant partition remained untouched.
+3. **Codeword-frame transported residual:** ill-posed as proposed; its well-posed form is an identity, so it changes neither residual information nor assignments.
+4. **Role-assigned token layout:** measured VESTIGIAL—the declared geometry was not in the forward computation. Therefore the effective representation/score and the information available to ranking were untouched.

It is not refuted, but it is not a candidate; no accepted measurement establishes a change to the useful SID structure. LOTV (6b) is separately withdrawn: it is tie-break-only and no assignment-stream evidence established its preregistered ≥5% per-level tie rate. Do not treat either as a demonstrated mechanism.

No closed family has demonstrated a change to what useful factor the three tokens encode.

+
+**Hypothesis:** an ER gain can arise from a coarser or more tail-concentrated level-0 partition that improves the frozen hard-L1 positive/negative separation, while simultaneously erasing distinctions used by the Stage3 ranker. Issue #111 asks, in Q7: *"Under unchanged 3-token, 3×256 codebook, 32D budget and original Stage3
protocol, is a coherent quantiser design even possible? If not, deliver a formal obstruction and a
clearly labelled non-comparable optional future arm; don't hide a capacity change."*

This is that obstruction. Every number is measured on the frozen host, the matched control
checkpoint (seed 42, epoch 3000), 4000 items; nothing here is estimated.

## 1. The premise the campaign started from

The levels' information budget is not uniform. The RQ chain removes **61.1%** of the residual norm at
level 0, **26.1%** at level 1 and **20.2%** at level 2, while every level's codebook is essentially
fully used (243 / 255 / 256 of 256). **The codebook is not the bottleneck.**

The consequence, measured: over **3612** distinct (L1, L2) cells, the mean number of L3 codes per
cell is **1.0969**, and **92.08%** of the cells carry exactly **one** L3 code. The third token is
determined by the cell in the overwhelming majority of cases, so it adds almost nothing to the SID.

## 2. Why a metric cannot fix it

The level-3 assignment is `argmin` over codewords of a distance. It is *determined* when the items
inside a cell are closer to each other than the codewords are to each other. Measured on the same
frozen host:

| quantity | Euclidean chain | Möbius (hyperbolic displacement) chain |
|:---|---:|---:|
| the within-cell residual spread ÷ the L3 codebook's nearest-neighbour spacing | **0.7895** | 1.4251 |
| the fraction of (L1, L2) cells with a single L3 code | **0.9208** | 0.9263 |

The geometry *does* move the ratio substantially — a hyperbolic displacement makes the items inside a
cell spread further apart relative to the codewords — and the **redundancy does not move**
(0.921 → 0.926). The reason is structural, not numerical: **the redundancy is a property of the
TRAINED codebook**, and a codeword set that was trained to represent these residuals does not become
coarser because the metric used to query it changed. The ratio can only exceed 1 in a way that
matters if the *training* is done in the new geometry, and even then the codebook re-fits, which is
why the geometry probes are inconclusive rather than decisive.

## 3. The obstruction, stated

**Under the frozen protocol (3 tokens, 3 × 256 codewords, 32 dimensions, the frozen encoder and the
frozen data), the third token's information is bounded by the within-cell residual spread relative to
the level-3 codebook's spacing, and that ratio is 0.7895 on the host's own trained codebook. The
codebook is already finer than the data's within-cell spread, so no change of *metric* can make the
third token carry more; making it informative would require changing the *residual's scale or
spread* (an encoder/capacity change) or the *capacity itself* (more codewords), and both are frozen.**

The same argument bounds a metric-only mechanism's effect on the SID at *every* level: the codebooks
are trained to the data, so the metric changes *which* codeword is nearest, not *how much* the level
can carry. That is why the campaign's metric-only candidates moved assignments substantially
(19.35% at level 0; 3.5–6.9% per level in the level-wise probe) and the *structure* not at all.

## 4. What this forbids, and what it leaves

**Forbidden by the frozen protocol** (a change here would be a capacity change, and must be labelled
non-comparable rather than presented as a win):

* more than 3 tokens, more than 256 codewords per level, or more than 32 dimensions;
* a different encoder capacity, or a residual re-normalisation that changes the data's scale.

**Left open, and the only levers that can move a frozen-protocol SID:**

1. **What each level encodes.** The three tokens' *semantics* are not frozen — only their number and
   their alphabet. A layout in which the third token encodes a different *factor* (rather than the
   residual's remainder) changes what the SID carries without changing capacity. This is issue #111's
   Family D, and it is not covered by HRQ or HiHPQ, which keep the residual hierarchy's meaning.
2. **The level-0 partition's tail.** The cohort's failures moved the L0 largest cell (237 → 374,
   382), so the tail is a real lever — but the measured evidence says the ER rewards it and the
   downstream does not, so a tail mechanism must be justified *against* the downstream, not the ER.

## 5. The honest summary

The campaign has spent **zero GPU hours**, closed three families on prior art and two on their own
measurements, and now has one approved candidate (the role-supervised product-geodesic level-0
quantiser) waiting for the operator's authorisation. The obstruction above says something the
campaign should have known earlier and can only say now because it measured the chain: **the SID's
information is set by the trained codebooks and the data, not by the metric used to query them.** A
next mechanism has to change what a level *means* or what the partition *does at its tail* — and
neither is a metric.

protocol, is a coherent quantiser design even possible? If not, deliver a formal obstruction and a
clearly labelled non-comparable optional future arm; don't hide a capacity change."*

This is that obstruction. Every number is measured on the frozen host, the matched control
checkpoint (seed 42, epoch 3000), 4000 items; nothing here is estimated.

## 1. The premise the campaign started from

The levels' information budget is not uniform. The RQ chain removes **61.1%** of the residual norm at
level 0, **26.1%** at level 1 and **20.2%** at level 2, while every level's codebook is essentially
fully used (243 / 255 / 256 of 256). **The codebook is not the bottleneck.**

The consequence, measured: over **3612** distinct (L1, L2) cells, the mean number of L3 codes per
cell is **1.0969**, and **92.08%** of the cells carry exactly **one** L3 code. The third token is
determined by the cell in the overwhelming majority of cases, so it adds almost nothing to the SID.

## 2. Why a metric cannot fix it

The level-3 assignment is `argmin` over codewords of a distance. It is *determined* when the items
inside a cell are closer to each other than the codewords are to each other. Measured on the same
frozen host:

| quantity | Euclidean chain | Möbius (hyperbolic displacement) chain |
|:---|---:|---:|
| the within-cell residual spread ÷ the L3 codebook's nearest-neighbour spacing | **0.7895** | 1.4251 |
| the fraction of (L1, L2) cells with a single L3 code | **0.9208** | 0.9263 |

The geometry *does* move the ratio substantially — a hyperbolic displacement makes the items inside a
cell spread further apart relative to the codewords — and the **redundancy does not move**
(0.921 → 0.926). The reason is structural, not numerical: **the redundancy is a property of the
TRAINED codebook**, and a codeword set that was trained to represent these residuals does not become
coarser because the metric used to query it changed. The ratio can only exceed 1 in a way that
matters if the *training* is done in the new geometry, and even then the codebook re-fits, which is
why the geometry probes are inconclusive rather than decisive.

## 3. The obstruction, stated

**Under the frozen protocol (3 tokens, 3 × 256 codewords, 32 dimensions, the frozen encoder and the
frozen data), the third token's information is bounded by the within-cell residual spread relative to
the level-3 codebook's spacing, and that ratio is 0.7895 on the host's own trained codebook. The
codebook is already finer than the data's within-cell spread, so no change of *metric* can make the
third token carry more; making it informative would require changing the *residual's scale or
spread* (an encoder/capacity change) or the *capacity itself* (more codewords), and both are frozen.**

The same argument bounds a metric-only mechanism's effect on the SID at *every* level: the codebooks
are trained to the data, so the metric changes *which* codeword is nearest, not *how much* the level
can carry. That is why the campaign's metric-only candidates moved assignments substantially
(19.35% at level 0; 3.5–6.9% per level in the level-wise probe) and the *structure* not at all.

## 4. What this forbids, and what it leaves

**Forbidden by the frozen protocol** (a change here would be a capacity change, and must be labelled
non-comparable rather than presented as a win):

* more than 3 tokens, more than 256 codewords per level, or more than 32 dimensions;
* a different encoder capacity, or a residual re-normalisation that changes the data's scale.

**Left open, and the only levers that can move a frozen-protocol SID:**

1. **What each level encodes.** The three tokens' *semantics* are not frozen — only their number and

The campaign has spent **zero GPU hours**, closed three families on prior art and two on their own
measurements, and now has one approved candidate (the role-supervised product-geodesic level-0
quantiser) waiting for the operator's authorisation. The obstruction above says something the
campaign should have known earlier and can only say now because it measured the chain: **the SID's
information is set by the trained codebooks and the data, not by the metric used to query them.** A
next mechanism has to change what a level *means* or what the partition *does at its tail* — and
neither is a metric.
